jurisdiction: European Union (EU-level framework + all 27 member states) — gambling/gaming licensing lane only. CORRECTED EDITION: this document applies the lane-3 adversarial audit. Where the audit refuted a claim, the refuted claim has been removed and replaced; where the audit raised a contested point, it is marked CONTESTED; where the audit found a decision-relevant omission, it is marked AUDIT ADDITION. Date of correction: 14 September 2026.
headline: There is no EU gambling licence and no EU gambling regulator — the Commission states flatly that there is no sector-specific EU legislation in the field of gambling services — so FACT//DUEL's money product must be licensed (or lawfully structured) state by state across 27 regimes. Model B (staking redeemable for cash) is not launchable as a pan-EU proposition: the EU definitions turn on stake + chance + prize, no member state accepts a dual paid-plus-free entry route as cleansing the paid route, and in the largest markets there is no licence class that fits a player-v-player knowledge stake. Model C (paid-entry knowledge contest) splits the Union three ways, but NOT along the lines the uncorrected brief drew: outside gambling law in Germany and Austria ONLY IF chance does not predominate — and in Germany a paid skill contest that escapes the GlueStV lands in § 33d GewO, which requires its own trade permit (AUDIT ADDITION; online application contested); contested-but-adverse in the Netherlands, where appellate authority has run against skill claims; LICENSABLE, NOT EXEMPT, in Sweden (Spellagen's kombinationsspel expressly covers skill-plus-chance games — the uncorrected brief's placement of Sweden outside gambling law was wrong), Ireland, Italy, Spain, Denmark and Malta; and caught in France because L320-1 CSI bites wherever ANY part of the gain is due to chance — France does not prohibit skill contests as a class, but FACT//DUEL's randomly drawn questions and reflex timers almost certainly put it inside the prohibition. Models A and D need no gambling licence anywhere, CONDITIONALLY: Model A becomes criminal exposure in Belgium if coins buy randomised rewards, and any competitive advantage bought by a Model D subscription converts it into Model C.

modelVerdicts.verdict: lawful — CONDITIONAL, not flat (audit correction: the original flat 'lawful in any member state' contradicted the brief's own Belgian criminal-exposure condition)
modelVerdicts.reasoning: Closed-loop coins that never convert to money or a prize of money's worth, and are never staked player-v-player, fail the prize/winnings limb of every EU-27 gambling definition and fail the 'wagering a stake' limb of the AMLR definition. On those facts no gambling licence is needed in any member state. THE VERDICT IS CONDITIONAL ON ALL FOUR OF THE FOLLOWING, and any one of them flips it: (1) the word 'entries' is load-bearing — if coins buy entry to anything carrying a prize of money or money's worth, Model A is Model C or B with a currency layer and is re-analysed there; (2) NO RANDOMISED PAID REWARDS. If coins buy loot boxes or gacha, Belgium is live criminal exposure: the Kansspelcommissie took the position in 2018 that paid virtual currency + chance + an item of value is illegal gambling under the Gaming Act of 7 May 1999. AUDIT CORRECTION: the 2018 output was a research report / position paper, not a formal adjudicative ruling, and its text remains UNVERIFIED; the position is nonetheless enforced by threat of criminal prosecution and the Netherlands has taken a comparable line. This is the one place Model A can become criminal; (3) EU consumer law applies regardless of gambling law: the CPC Network's seven principles on in-game virtual currencies (adopted 21 March 2025, with coordinated enforcement opened the same day against Star Stable Entertainment AB) require real-money price display, no forced currency bundling, and respect for the withdrawal right; the Digital Fairness Act is on the Commission work programme for Q4 2026 with virtual currencies and loot boxes expressly in scope (the audit contested this as possibly Q3 2026; the editor checked the European Parliament Legislative Train file, which records the DFA under 'Protecting our democracy, upholding our values' as a Q4 2026 legislative initiative — Q4 2026 RETAINED); (4) AUDIT ADDITION: minor-protection and age-assurance duties apply to Model A independently of gambling law — the DSA's minor-protection provisions, German JuSchG and national youth-media law. Not analysed in this lane; UNVERIFIED as to specifics.

modelVerdicts.verdict: not launchable as a pan-EU proposition — unlicensable in the largest markets, licence-required in a minority, nowhere lawful unlicensed
modelVerdicts.reasoning: The US sweepstakes-casino structure survives because US law requires 'consideration', which a free alternative method of entry negates. AUDIT CORRECTION — the uncorrected brief said 'no EU member state uses that gateway', which is wrong and would mislead a founder into dismissing free-entry designs that do work in specific states. Every EU definition turns on a stake or payment limb, which is the functional analogue of consideration: Germany's § 3(1) GlueStV asks whether an Entgelt is demanded, and Spellagen 3 kap. 4 § expressly provides that 'licens kravs inte for spel dar deltagande inte kraver betalning av en insats' — no licence for games requiring no stake. A genuinely free-to-enter product is outside gambling law in several states. THE DEFENSIBLE NARROW POINT is that no EU state accepts a DUAL paid-plus-free entry route as cleansing the paid route, and France pre-empts it in terms: L320-1 CSI deems financial sacrifice established 'meme si un remboursement ulterieur est rendu possible par le reglement du jeu'. Beyond definitions, the second wall is that in most states NO LICENCE CLASS FITS a player-v-player trivia stake. Germany: AUDIT CORRECTION — the uncorrected brief's list of GGL permission classes was presented as exhaustive and was not. GlueStV 2021 made licensable virtuelle Automatenspiele, Online-Poker UND ONLINECASINOSPIELE; online casino games are authorised by the individual Laender under their own concession procedures, not by the GGL, which handles sports betting, virtual slots and online poker. The corrected German conclusion is narrower but survives: there is still no permission class for a P2P knowledge stake, so the product cannot be licensed in its current shape — but 'unlicensable' should be read as 'no fitting class today', not as a structural bar to any restructuring into a licensable class. Poland reserves online casino to Totalizator Sportowy. Austria's online monopoly sits with Oesterreichische Lotterien pending reform (reform details CONTESTED, see subdivisions). Cyprus prohibits online casino. Slovenia reserves most online verticals to Loterija Slovenije and Sportna loterija. Belgium ties online licences to land-based venues. Where a fitting class DOES exist the verdict is licence-required, not lawful: Malta (Type 3 for P2P with a rake — but see the Malta characterisation warning), Italy under a D.Lgs. 41/2024 concession, Spain via a general + singular licence, Denmark, Sweden, the Netherlands, Ireland, Portugal, Greece, Romania, Czechia and most CEE states. None of those licences reach beyond their own borders. AUDIT ADDITION — THE RAKE IS THE STRUCTURAL LEVER, and it is bigger than the timer: whether FACT//DUEL takes a commission from a player-funded pot (which is what makes it Type 3 P2P in Malta and a 'stake' in most definitions) or pays a fixed announced prize pool out of its own funds (which in several states removes the stake limb from the player side entirely) is the difference between licensable and out-of-scope in Germany, Austria and the Netherlands. This was absent from the uncorrected brief and must be decided before any legal opinion is commissioned. AUDIT ADDITION — PAYMENTS: any model with a cash-out requires holding and remitting player funds, which triggers PSD2/EMD2 authorisation or a regulated PSP/e-money partner, plus player-fund segregation obligations that are licence conditions in DK, NL, SE, ES and MT. Specifics UNVERIFIED; out of this lane but a hard build dependency.

modelVerdicts.verdict: unsettled — and the split does NOT run where the uncorrected brief said it did
modelVerdicts.reasoning: This is the only model where the honest answer is that the EU has no single answer. THREE CAMPS, AS CORRECTED. Camp 1 — outside GAMBLING law where chance does not predominate, but not therefore unregulated: GERMANY (§ 3(1) GlueStV 2021 requires the win decision to depend 'ganz oder ueberwiegend vom Zufall'; a contest decided by intellectual performance is not Gluecksspiel even with an entry fee, and § 284 StGB does not bite — entry-fee commentary is SECONDARY, IHK/law-firm notes). AUDIT ADDITION AND THE SINGLE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL OMISSION IN THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF: escaping § 3(1) GlueStV does not mean no German permission is required. § 33d GewO requires an Erlaubnis from the competent authority for commercially operating 'andere Spiele mit Gewinnmoeglichkeit' — other games with a chance to win that are NOT Gluecksspiel — which is precisely the category a paid skill contest falls into when it escapes the GlueStV; the permit requires an Unbedenklichkeitsbescheinigung from the Bundeskriminalamt and can be refused for unreliability (editor verified the provision's existence and content at gesetze-im-internet.de). Its application to a purely online offering is CONTESTED and unsettled — which is exactly why it must be in a German legal opinion. The uncorrected brief's advice line was 'run Model C in Germany unlicensed'; that advice is withdrawn. AUSTRIA (GSpG 1989 § 1(1), 'ausschliesslich oder vorwiegend vom Zufall' — statutory text UNVERIFIED, not fetched by researcher or auditor); AUDIT ADDITION: Austrian Preisausschreiben / prize-competition rules and national unfair-commercial-practice rules on paid entry contests still apply — UNVERIFIED as to detail. Camp 1-CONTESTED — NETHERLANDS: the uncorrected brief placed the Netherlands in Camp 1 on the basis that Dutch courts 'have gone both ways', citing a 2010 Hague District Court decision as live counter-authority. AUDIT CORRECTION: that decision was reversed on appeal by the Gerechtshof Den Haag and Dutch higher courts have consistently maintained that poker is a kansspel under the Wok. The honest framing is that the 'overwegende invloed' test has been applied AGAINST skill claims at appellate level, which makes the Netherlands materially less favourable than a 50/50. Wok Art. 1(1)(a) text remains UNVERIFIED (not fetched). AUDIT ADDITION: the Dutch Gedragscode promotionele kansspelen applies to promotional games outside the Wok. Camp 2 — LICENCE REQUIRED EVEN WHERE SKILL PREDOMINATES: SWEDEN — MOVED HERE FROM CAMP 1 BY THE AUDIT, and this is the correction most likely to change a launch decision. Spellagen defines kombinationsspel as 'spel dar deltagarna har chans att vinna ett pris och dar sannolikheten att vinna beror pa en kombination av skicklighet och slump' — a game where the participant may win a prize and the chance of winning depends on a combination of skill and chance — and kombinationsspel is a licensable form of spel, structurally identical to the Danish kombinationsspil the brief already treated as fatal (editor verified the definition against the Spellag text). The Spelinspektionen guidance the brief relied on exempts only competitions decided by a prestationsmoment 'utan inslag av lottning eller slump' — WITHOUT any element of chance. A randomly drawn question set introduces exactly that element. On its own facts FACT//DUEL's paid duel is a candidate Swedish kombinationsspel requiring a Spelinspektionen licence. IRELAND ('a game of skill or chance, or partly of skill and partly of chance' + payment + prize of money's worth — s. 2 definitions SECONDARY, irishstatutebook.ie 403 to researcher and auditor); ITALY (D.M. 17 settembre 2007 n. 186 regulates giochi di abilita a distanza con vincita in denaro — remote skill games with cash prizes, expressly games where the result depends on skill predominantly over the random element — ADM concession required; AUDIT ADDITION: D.Lgs. 41/2024 sets a multi-million-euro per-concession fee, widely reported around EUR 7m for a nine-year concession, UNVERIFIED, and Italy operates a near-total gambling advertising ban under the Decreto Dignita — either fact alone removes Italy from an early-stage footprint); SPAIN (see the corrected Spain analysis — skill-predominance is no defence ONCE A CHANCE ELEMENT IS PRESENT, which is narrower than 'no pure-skill exemption'); DENMARK (Spilleloven § 5 kombinationsspil); MALTA (controlled skill games under the Gaming Act Cap. 583 and MGA Directive 6 of 2018 — NOT under S.L. 438.11, which is repealed; see the Malta correction). Camp 3 — CAUGHT IN FRANCE, but for the right reason: AUDIT CORRECTION — the uncorrected brief said France is 'specifically a no to skill games' as a class. On the brief's own quoted text, L320-1 CSI catches operations offered to the public 'pour faire naitre l'esperance d'un gain qui serait du, meme partiellement, au hasard' where a financial sacrifice is required. CHANCE REMAINS A CONSTITUENT ELEMENT. The savoir-faire sentence closes the skill-PREDOMINANCE escape for mixed games; it does not prohibit paid contests decided wholly by knowledge or ability, and paid chess and bridge tournaments and quiz competitions continue lawfully in France. The correct statement is that France catches any contest with ANY chance element — which on FACT//DUEL's own facts (randomly drawn questions, reflex timers) probably does catch it. The video-game competition carve-out at Arts. L321-8 to L321-11 CSI (Decret n° 2017-871 of 9 May 2017) applies only to competitions with participants physically present, so it is not a route. THE PRODUCT-SPECIFIC KILLER SURVIVES THE AUDIT UNCHANGED: FACT//DUEL's 5/7/10-second timers on randomly drawn questions materially shift outcome determination toward chance. A German, Austrian or Dutch regulator assessing skill predominance will look at question randomisation, timer length and sample size per contest. One duel over a handful of 5-second questions is a far weaker skill case than a 50-question fixed set. Second only to the rake structure, this is the highest-leverage design variable in the EU analysis.

modelVerdicts.verdict: lawful — CONDITIONAL on the subscription conferring no competitive advantage in any prize contest
modelVerdicts.reasoning: A recurring fee for features or cosmetics, with no stake and no prize of money or money's worth, is not gambling in any of the 27. No gambling licence anywhere. ONE TRAP, specific to this product: a subscription can itself constitute the consideration that turns an otherwise-free contest into gambling. The MGA's definition of fantasy sports — the archetype for controlled skill games — counts consideration 'whether in the form of a stake, a periodic subscription or the purchase of in-game items, which provides an advantage to the player' (SECONDARY, via MGA/Legal 500 restatement of Directive 6 of 2018). So if the FACT//DUEL subscription grants extra expedition entries, better odds, higher stake tiers, or any competitive advantage in a prize event, it is a paid entry and the analysis flips to Model C or B. Keep it strictly cosmetic and strictly orthogonal to any prize contest. AUDIT CORRECTION — the uncorrected brief said of Model D that 'no gambling-law authority is engaged' and stopped there. That is incomplete: EU consumer law bites regardless (Digital Content Directive (EU) 2019/770, the Consumer Rights Directive 14-day withdrawal right, the CPC virtual-currency principles of 21 March 2025), and AUDIT ADDITION — age verification and minor-protection duties apply independently of gambling law (DSA minor-protection provisions, German JuSchG, national youth-media law), including for a subscription sold to minors. Specifics UNVERIFIED and out of this lane.

checklist.item: Accept and design around the fact that there is no EU gambling licence and no mutual recognition — budget for per-member-state licensing, not one EU authorisation
checklist.issuer: European Commission (DG GROW) / CJEU
checklist.notes: The Commission's online gambling page states that there is no sector-specific EU legislation in the field of gambling services and that EU countries are autonomous in how they organise gambling services. CJEU Case C-440/23 — AUDIT FLAGGED THIS AS POSSIBLY FABRICATED; THE EDITOR CHECKED AND THE CASE IS REAL. It is European Lotto and Betting Ltd and Deutsche Lotto- und Sportwetten Ltd, judgment of 16 April 2026, following AG Emiliou's opinion of 4 September 2025 (CELEX 62023CC0440). Holdings as reported across GTG Advocates, Gecic Law, Mondaq, BSP and AGB: EU law does not preclude a member state prohibiting online gambling services authorised in another member state; member states may attach civil-law consequences including nullity of contracts and restitution of lost stakes; a player's restitution claim is not an abuse of EU rights. The underlying facts were Malta-licensed operators serving German players between June 2019 and July 2021. The judgment text itself was not fetched from curia.europa.eu — the holdings are corroborated across multiple independent practitioner sources but remain SECONDARY as to exact wording.

checklist.item: Decide the launch shape FIRST: Model A/D (no gambling licence anywhere) vs Model C (split 27 ways, and not where you thought) vs Model B (do not attempt in the EU)
checklist.issuer: Founder / board decision
checklist.notes: Recommended EU sequencing: ship Model A + Model D EU-wide now with zero gambling licensing (subject to the Model A conditions — no randomised paid rewards anywhere, Belgium especially); treat Model C as a licensed-market product state by state; drop Model B for the EU. CORRECTED: the sweepstakes structure fails in the EU not because 'no consideration gateway exists' (several states DO exempt genuinely free-to-enter games — Spellagen 3 kap. 4 § is explicit) but because no member state accepts a DUAL paid-plus-free entry route as cleansing the paid route, and France defeats it in terms via L320-1 CSI. A genuinely free-only product is a different and possibly viable design; a paid product with a free side door is not.

checklist.item: Geo-block France for any paid-entry contest or staking product, and geo-block it hard (IP + payment BIN + device)
checklist.issuer: ANJ (Autorite Nationale des Jeux)
checklist.prerequisite: Server-authoritative geolocation at account and transaction level
checklist.notes: CORRECTED RATIONALE. L320-1 CSI catches operations offered to the public to create the hope of a gain due EVEN PARTIALLY to chance where a financial sacrifice is required, and adds that the prohibition covers games whose operation rests on the players' savoir-faire. France therefore catches any paid contest with ANY chance element — it does NOT prohibit skill contests as a class (paid chess, bridge and quiz competitions continue lawfully). The geo-block conclusion is unchanged for FACT//DUEL because randomly drawn questions and reflex timers supply the chance element, but the reason matters: a fully deterministic, fixed-question, no-timer format is not automatically illegal in France and would need French counsel rather than a blanket assumption. The video-game competition carve-out at Arts. L321-8 to L321-11 CSI requires PHYSICAL PRESENCE of participants. ANJ licences exist only for sports betting, horse betting and online poker. L320-1 WORDING WAS NEVER FETCHED FROM LEGIFRANCE (403) BY EITHER THE RESEARCHER OR THE AUDITOR — confirm the consolidated wording with French counsel.

checklist.leadTime: UNVERIFIED — consultancies quote 4-6 months for a clean application and 6-12 months for complex ownership or novel products; the MGA publishes no service-level commitment that could be verified. Treat consultancy figures as marketing material.

Do not cite S.L. 438.11. checklist.item: Choose the MGA licence type: Type 4 (controlled skill game) if the MGA will classify a knowledge duel as one; Type 3 (P2P, operator takes commission) if it will not — AND UNDERSTAND THAT THIS CHOICE IS AN EU-WIDE CHARACTERISATION, NOT A FORM-FILLING DECISION
checklist.issuer: Malta Gaming Authority
checklist.cost: Fixed annual licence fee: EUR 10,000 if providing SOLELY Type 4 services; EUR 25,000 for a B2C Gaming Service Licence otherwise (incl. Type 3). Minimum share capital: Type 4 EUR 40,000, Type 3 EUR 40,000, Types 1-2 EUR 100,000
checklist.prerequisite: MGA application accepted; game design documentation demonstrating that skill determines the outcome alone or predominantly
checklist.notes: AUDIT CORRECTION — THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF RECOMMENDED TYPE 3 AS THE 'LIKELIER FIT' WITHOUT FLAGGING THE CONSEQUENCE. Type 3 is, on the MGA's own definition, a class of GAMES OF CHANCE ('games of chance not played against the house and wherein the operator is not exposed to gaming risk'). Applying for Type 3 concedes that the product is a game of chance — which destroys the skill-predominance argument in Germany and Austria, weakens it in the Netherlands, and strengthens capture in Denmark, Spain, Ireland, Sweden and Italy. Type 3 and Type 4 are NOT interchangeable fallbacks. If the EU strategy depends on Model C being outside gambling law anywhere, do not file for Type 3. Type 4 = controlled skill games. CRITICAL GAP (unchanged by the audit): under Directive 6 of 2018 (Controlled Skill Games Ruling, 1 August 2018) FANTASY SPORTS IS THE ONLY GAME THE MGA HAS CLASSIFIED as a controlled skill game; a trivia duel needs a fresh MGA determination, so budget for a pre-application ruling request. The burden of proving skill predominance is on the applicant. The reg. 8 Gaming Authorisations Regulations cross-reference could not be verified against primary text by either the researcher or the auditor; the auditor notes the Gaming Authorisations Regulations are S.L. 583.05 — REGULATION NUMBER UNVERIFIED.

GAMING TAX: the audit flagged this as possibly fabricated; THE EDITOR CHECKED AND IT IS REAL — PwC Malta ('Changes in Gaming Tax applicable from October 2026'), the MGA's own 'Enhancements to Malta's VAT and Gaming Tax Frameworks' announcement and an MTCA government press release all confirm the Gaming Tax (Amendment) Regulations 2026 coming into force 1 October 2026, with 15% for Type 1 and 10% for Types 2-4. THE EXACT LEGAL NOTICE NUMBERS (reported as LN 84/2026 and LN 86/2026) REMAIN UNVERIFIED — do not cite them. MATERIAL FACT THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF MISSED ENTIRELY: for distance gaming the taxability test is being changed from the player's PHYSICAL PRESENCE in Malta to whether the player is established, has a permanent address and/or usually resides in Malta. The old 'only players physically in Malta' rule of thumb no longer states the rule and the base may be wider for a consumer app with Maltese-resident users. The device-based levy is abolished and a higher fixed studio broadcasting levy introduced. A separate VAT change also takes effect 1 October 2026 — OUT OF LANE, UNANALYSED. Start-ups qualifying under the MGA's Start-Up Undertakings Directive get a 12-month compliance-contribution moratorium.

checklist.notes: THIS ITEM IS THE MOST CHANGED IN THE DOCUMENT. The uncorrected brief's advice was 'run Model C in Germany unlicensed'. That advice is WITHDRAWN. CORRECTED PICTURE: (1) GlueStV 2021 permission classes are NOT limited to sports betting (§ 21), online poker (§ 22b), virtual slot machines (§ 22a), lotteries and horse betting — the GGL's own legal-basis page states GlueStV 2021 made licensable virtuelle Automatenspiele, Online-Poker UND ONLINECASINOSPIELE, and online casino games are authorised by the individual LAENDER under their own concession procedures, not by the GGL. There is still no class that fits a P2P knowledge stake, so Model B cannot be licensed in its current shape, but the word 'unlicensable' was overstated — restructuring into a licensable class is not categorically foreclosed. (2) Model C that escapes § 3(1) GlueStV does NOT thereby escape German permission requirements: § 33d GewO requires an Erlaubnis for the commercial operation of 'andere Spiele mit Gewinnmoeglichkeit' — other games with a chance to win that are not Gluecksspiel — with a Bundeskriminalamt Unbedenklichkeitsbescheinigung as a precondition and refusal mandated where the applicant lacks reliability (provision verified at gesetze-im-internet.de, 14 Sep 2026). ITS APPLICATION TO PURELY ONLINE OFFERINGS IS CONTESTED and is the exact question the German opinion must answer. (3) GET THE OPINION ON THE 5/7/10-SECOND TIMER AND THE RANDOM QUESTION DRAW before relying on the skill analysis at all. Statutory evaluation of GlueStV 2021 is due by 31 December 2026 under § 32 (section number SECONDARY); a successor treaty would not take effect before 2027-2028 (SECONDARY, trade press). No 2025 or 2026 amendment to GlueStV 2021 appears on the GGL's legal-basis page.

checklist.item: Apply for a Spanish DGOJ general licence in the 'concursos' (or 'otros juegos') category plus the matching singular licence
checklist.issuer: Direccion General de Ordenacion del Juego (DGOJ), Spain
checklist.leadTime: UNVERIFIED — general licences are granted through a public convocatoria, not on demand; timing depends on the DGOJ opening a round
checklist.prerequisite: General licence must be held before the corresponding singular licence can be requested
checklist.notes: CORRECTED ON TWO POINTS. (1) The uncorrected brief said 'Spain expressly has NO pure-skill exemption'. That overstates Art. 3(a) Ley 13/2011, which requires the uncertain future results to be 'dependientes EN ALGUNA MEDIDA DEL AZAR' — dependent to some degree on chance. The 'con independencia de que predomine... el grado de habilidad' clause means skill-predominance is no defence ONCE A CHANCE ELEMENT IS PRESENT; it does not capture a contest with no chance element at all. For FACT//DUEL the practical answer is the same (random question draw supplies the chance element) but the reasoning must be stated correctly. (2) THE GENERAL-LICENCE CATEGORIES (apuestas, rifas, concursos, otros juegos) SIT IN ARTICLE 10, NOT ARTICLE 9 — the uncorrected brief's authority line was wrong. 'Concursos' is defined at Art. 3(e) as offers made through media (TV/radio/internet) requiring an economic outlay with prizes determined by chance, competition or knowledge tests; WHETHER AN APP-BASED DUEL FITS THAT DEFINITION IS UNTESTED AND UNVERIFIED and is a specific question for Spanish counsel. Art. 2.2 excludes only games of puro ocio, pasatiempo o recreo constituting usos sociales with no economically evaluable transfers. AUDIT ADDITION: Spain's Real Decreto 958/2020 imposes severe gambling advertising restrictions, and player-winnings withholding tax and gambling VAT treatment change prize-pool economics — both UNVERIFIED as to detail and both capable of making a licensed Spanish product unmarketable. The DGOJ was consulting on Ley 13/2011 amendments as at July 2026 — SECONDARY.

checklist.item: Apply for an ADM concession in Italy if you want Italian players in any paid contest — but price the concession before planning on it
checklist.issuer: Agenzia delle Dogane e dei Monopoli (ADM), Italy
checklist.cost: NOT 'UNVERIFIED' IN THE SENSE OF UNKNOWN-BUT-SMALL. AUDIT ADDITION: D.Lgs. 41/2024 sets a multi-million-euro fee per remote concession, widely reported at around EUR 7m for a nine-year concession — FIGURE UNVERIFIED but the order of magnitude is the decision-relevant fact. Treat Italy as out of reach for an early-stage product until this is confirmed.
checklist.leadTime: UNVERIFIED — the 2024-25 reordering tender is closed. Reports that ADM awarded 52 concessions to 46 operators in September 2025 with each operator capped at 5 concessions are SECONDARY AND UNVERIFIED (the auditor could not confirm the counts).
checklist.prerequisite: Wait for or qualify under a future ADM bando
checklist.notes: Italy explicitly regulates skill games with cash prizes rather than exempting them: D.M. 17 settembre 2007 n. 186, 'Regolamento per la disciplina dei giochi di abilita a distanza con vincita in denaro', covers games where the result depends PREDOMINANTLY OVER the random element on player skill — so demonstrating skill predominance in Italy puts you INSIDE the licensing regime, not outside it. The remote sector was reordered by D.Lgs. 25 marzo 2024 n. 41, in force 4 April 2024. AUDIT ADDITION — ADVERTISING: Italy operates a near-total gambling advertising ban under the Decreto Dignita. A licensed Model C in Italy could be legal to operate and impossible to market. For a consumer app that is decisive, and it was entirely absent from the uncorrected brief.

checklist.item: Apply for a Dutch KSA remote gambling licence if you want Model B; Model C MAY fall outside the Wok but the appellate weather is against you
checklist.issuer: Kansspelautoriteit (KSA), Netherlands
checklist.notes: CORRECTED. Wok Art. 1(1)(a): gambling exists where winners are determined by a chance mechanism on which participants cannot generally exert decisive influence ('overwegende invloed'); a genuine behendigheidsspel falls outside. The uncorrected brief presented this as a live 50/50 by citing a 2010 Hague District Court decision against the 1998 Hoge Raad poker ruling. AUDIT CORRECTION: the 2010 decision was REVERSED ON APPEAL by the Gerechtshof Den Haag and Dutch higher courts have consistently held poker to be a kansspel. The test has been applied AGAINST skill claims at appellate level. The Netherlands is materially less favourable for Model C than the uncorrected brief implied. Wok statutory text was never fetched (SECONDARY). Current licensing: new policy rules BVRKOA 2026 in force 1 January 2026; the September 2021 cohort of licences EXPIRES 1 OCTOBER 2026 (a FUTURE event as at 14 September 2026 — the uncorrected brief's risks section stated this in the completed past tense); licences run a maximum of 5 years; applicants must file an exit plan and a change-notification plan. The KSA's 2026 Toezichtagenda prioritises illegal supply through an alliance with payment providers, social media and hosting parties. AUDIT ADDITION: the Dutch Gedragscode promotionele kansspelen governs promotional games that sit outside the Wok, and the Netherlands operates an untargeted-gambling-advertising ban — UNVERIFIED as to detail.

checklist.item: Track the Irish GRAI remote gaming licence window and apply when it opens — but treat every Irish date in this document as provisional
checklist.issuer: Gambling Regulatory Authority of Ireland (GRAI)
checklist.cost: UNVERIFIED — the Gambling Regulation Act 2024 leaves fees to be prescribed by the GRAI with the Minister's consent, so NO FEE FIGURE SHOULD BE BUDGETED. The pre-existing remote bookmaker regime's EUR 10,000 fee and EUR 10,000-200,000 biennial renewals are SECONDARY and are not the new regime's fees.
checklist.prerequisite: Irish or in-scope entity; fit-and-proper declarations for every relevant officer and beneficial owner; tax clearance
checklist.notes: Ireland matters because its definition of gaming expressly catches skill: 'games of skill or chance (or partly of skill and partly of chance) where the participant pays money for the chance to win a prize of money (or money's worth)'. CONTESTED / PROVISIONAL PER AUDIT: none of the commencement dates or exemption thresholds could be verified by either the researcher or the auditor — irishstatutebook.ie, oireachtas.ie and grai.ie all returned 403. The reported timeline (commencement order signed 3 February 2026, effective 5 February 2026; remote betting applications opened 9 February 2026; remote betting licence requirement from 1 July 2026; in-person from 1 December 2026) and the reported exemption thresholds (one-off charitable lotteries under EUR 2,000; marketing lotteries capped at EUR 5,000) are ALL UNVERIFIED — the betting dates are corroborated across DLA Piper, LexisNexis and gov.ie, which is better than nothing but is still secondary. The s. 2 definitions on which the whole Irish verdict turns are quoted only through a law-firm guide. REMOTE GAMING (B2C) LICENCES ARE REPORTED AS NOT YET OPEN, variously Q4 2026 or 2027-28 — confirm directly with the GRAI Operator Portal before any Irish planning. Administrative sanctions are reported at up to EUR 20m or 10% of turnover (UNVERIFIED).

checklist.item: Apply for a Danish Spillemyndigheden licence for any paid contest with Danish players
checklist.issuer: Spillemyndigheden, Denmark
checklist.notes: Spilleloven § 5 defines 'kombinationsspil' as activities where the chance of winning depends on 'en kombination af faerdighed og tilfaeldighed' — skill AND chance combined — and these require a licence. Only games decided purely by skill fall outside the Act. A trivia duel with randomly drawn questions is a textbook kombinationsspil. Spillemyndigheden's public guidance: charge for participation and you need permission; make it free and you do not. Danish statutory text was fetched from danskelove.dk. NOTE THE READ-ACROSS THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF MISSED: Sweden has the structurally identical kombinationsspel concept, which is why Sweden has been moved out of the 'no licence' camp in this corrected edition.

checklist.item: Apply for a Spelinspektionen licence for any paid contest with Swedish players — SWEDEN IS A LICENCE MARKET FOR THIS PRODUCT, NOT AN EXEMPT ONE
checklist.issuer: Spelinspektionen, Sweden
checklist.prerequisite: Swedish legal opinion on whether the duel is a kombinationsspel
checklist.notes: AUDIT-DRIVEN REVERSAL — THIS ITEM REPLACES THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF'S PLACEMENT OF SWEDEN OUTSIDE GAMBLING LAW. Spellagen defines kombinationsspel as 'spel dar deltagarna har chans att vinna ett pris och dar sannolikheten att vinna beror pa en kombination av skicklighet och slump' — a game where participants have a chance to win a prize and the probability of winning depends on a COMBINATION OF SKILL AND CHANCE — and kombinationsspel is a licensable form of spel (definition verified against the Spellag text, 14 Sep 2026). The Spelinspektionen guidance the uncorrected brief relied on exempts only competitions decided by a prestationsmoment 'utan inslag av lottning eller slump' — WITHOUT any element of drawing lots or chance. A randomly drawn question set is exactly that element. A Swedish Model C would therefore need either a Spelinspektionen licence or a format with an identical fixed question set for every entrant, no random matching and no chance-introducing timer, and even then a Swedish opinion. Other exemptions at 3 kap. 4-5 §§ Spellagen: free-to-enter games (no stake), private play between close connections, combination games in periodicals/radio/TV, and municipal non-profit lotteries. An amending act SFS 2025:767 exists and ITS CONTENT IS UNVERIFIED — it could affect this position.

checklist.item: Run the Model C skill-predominance test as a DESIGN requirement, not a legal afterthought — lengthen timers, enlarge the question set, fix the prize pool, and log the evidence
checklist.issuer: Self-imposed (evidence for DE/AT/NL regulators, a Swedish or Danish licence application, and an MGA Type 4 determination)
checklist.notes: The variables that decide whether chance predominates: (1) timer length — 5 seconds converts knowledge into reflex and randomness; (2) question randomisation — a random draw per duel injects chance the German, Austrian, Dutch, Swedish and Danish tests all weigh; (3) sample size — one duel over a handful of questions has high variance, a 50-question fixed set does not; (4) opponent matching — random matching adds chance, skill-banded matching removes it; (5) an identical question set for all entrants in an expedition removes draw-luck entirely and is a hard requirement for any Swedish or French argument. Keep per-player telemetry showing that higher-knowledge players win at a rate materially above chance; in Malta the burden of proof is expressly on the applicant.

checklist.item: DECIDE THE RAKE STRUCTURE BEFORE ANY LEGAL OPINION IS COMMISSIONED — operator-funded fixed prize pool vs commission on a player-funded pot
checklist.issuer: Founder / product (AUDIT ADDITION — absent from the uncorrected brief)
checklist.notes: AUDIT ADDITION, AND A BIGGER LEVER THAN THE TIMER. The uncorrected brief never analysed whether FACT//DUEL takes a commission from a player-funded pot or pays a fixed announced prize pool from its own funds. Taking a rake from a player-funded pot is what makes the product a Type 3 P2P game in Malta and a 'stake' under most EU definitions. Paying a fixed, announced, operator-funded prize pool that does not depend on the number of entrants — which is exactly what Model C is defined as — removes or weakens the stake limb on the player side in several states and is the difference between licensable and out-of-scope in Germany, Austria and the Netherlands. Model C as defined in this project (fixed prize pool announced in advance, funded by the operator, NOT dependent on entrant numbers) is the favourable structure; any drift toward pot-splitting converts it into Model B. Note that the entry FEE may still constitute a stake in states whose test is 'is an Entgelt demanded for a Gewinnchance' (Germany) regardless of who funds the pool — CONTESTED and a question for each local opinion.

checklist.item: Build to the AMLR (Regulation (EU) 2024/1624) now — it applies directly from 10 July 2027 and gives the first EU-wide definition of a gambling service
checklist.issuer: National AML supervisors; Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA), Frankfurt
checklist.appliesTo: B, C (and Model A only if 'entries' carry a prize of value)
checklist.prerequisite: Identity/KYC stack, transaction monitoring, attribution of transactions to a customer before identity verification
checklist.notes: CORRECTED ON THREE POINTS, TWO OF THEM CITATION ERRORS IN AN ITEM THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF LABELLED 'VERIFIED PRIMARY TEXT'. (1) THE CDD PROVISION IS ARTICLE 19(5), NOT ARTICLE 20(5). Art. 19 ('Application of customer due diligence measures'), para. 5: 'providers of gambling services shall apply customer due diligence measures upon the collection of winnings, the wagering of a stake, or both, when carrying out transactions amounting to at least EUR 2 000'. Article 20 is the article listing the CDD MEASURES themselves; Art. 19(5) cross-refers to 'Article 20(1), point (a)'. Recital 64 confirms the threshold can be met by several linked smaller transactions. (2) THE ART. 4 EXEMPTION IS NOT THE CLOSED DOOR THE BRIEF DESCRIBED. The brief truncated Art. 4(1) mid-sentence. The text continues after 'online gambling services or sport betting services' with: 'other than: (i) online gambling services operated by the State... (ii) online gambling services the organisation, operation and administration of which is regulated by the State', and recital 63 confirms the carve-back. An operator inside a state-regulated online regime is NOT automatically outside the exemption. Art. 4 exemptions also require a Member State risk assessment and (per recital 63) a Commission approval/rejection step. The flat statement 'FACT//DUEL under Model B or C cannot be exempted' is WITHDRAWN. (3) AMLR CAPTURE OF MODEL C IS NOT SETTLED. Art. 2(1)(12) defines a gambling service as one 'which involves wagering a stake with monetary value in GAMES OF CHANCE, including those with an element of skill'. The chance limb is still required; 'including those with an element of skill' extends the definition to mixed games, it does not abolish it for skill-predominant ones. A Model C contest with genuinely no chance element is ARGUABLY NOT an AMLR gambling service — and the brief cannot simultaneously argue that Model C is chance-free enough to escape § 3(1) GlueStV and that it is an AMLR game of chance. CONTESTED; resolve it with counsel, and note that the safe engineering assumption is still to build the KYC and transaction-attribution stack, because retrofitting it is far more expensive than building it. Art. 3, point (3)(g) makes providers of gambling services obliged entities.

checklist.item: Comply with the CPC Network in-game virtual currency principles and prepare for the Digital Fairness Act
checklist.issuer: CPC Network (national consumer authorities, coordinated by the European Commission)
checklist.leadTime: Principles in effect since 21 March 2025; Digital Fairness Act on the Commission work programme for Q4 2026
checklist.notes: Seven principles adopted 21 March 2025: show the real-money value of every in-game purchase, no practices that hide costs or force currency bundling, respect the withdrawal right, protect minors and vulnerable users. Coordinated enforcement was opened the same day against Star Stable Entertainment AB for direct exhortation to children, time-limited purchase pressure, and insufficient transparency about virtual-currency spending. These apply to Model A and Model D even though no gambling law does. DIGITAL FAIRNESS ACT TIMING: the audit contested the Q4 2026 date, suggesting the Commission's programming documents indicated Q3 2026. THE EDITOR CHECKED: the European Parliament's Legislative Train Schedule file records the DFA as a Q4 2026 legislative initiative under 'Protecting our democracy, upholding our values'. Q4 2026 IS RETAINED. As at 14 September 2026 the proposal has therefore NOT yet been tabled; the reported scope (dark patterns, addictive design, loot boxes, virtual currencies, influencer marketing, personalised pricing) and the reported possibility of an outright loot-box ban or a parental-consent requirement for minors are SECONDARY and pre-legislative.

checklist.item: Do NOT rely on an MGA licence to reach other EU markets — it does not passport, and C-440/23 now makes the downside a restitution liability
checklist.issuer: CJEU / Malta Gaming Authority
checklist.notes: There is no mutual recognition of gaming licences in EU law. Malta's Bill 55 (2023), inserting Art. 56A into the Gaming Act, requires Maltese courts to refuse recognition of foreign judgments against MGA licensees; the Commission issued a letter of formal notice on Art. 56A. CJEU Case C-440/23 (European Lotto and Betting Ltd and Deutsche Lotto- und Sportwetten Ltd), judgment 16 April 2026, held that EU law does not preclude a member state prohibiting online gambling services authorised in another member state, that member states may attach civil-law consequences including contract nullity and restitution of lost stakes, and that a player's restitution claim is not an abuse of EU rights. THE AUDIT FLAGGED THIS CASE AS POSSIBLY FABRICATED; THE EDITOR VERIFIED IT EXISTS AND THE HOLDINGS ARE AS DESCRIBED, corroborated across GTG Advocates, Gecic Law, Mondaq, BSP and AGB. The judgment text was NOT fetched from curia.europa.eu, so exact wording remains SECONDARY. Bill 55 does not shield you from a German, Dutch or Austrian claim. The underlying no-mutual-recognition principle is independently sound on older authority (Schindler, Laeaerae, Zenatti, Placanica, Gambelli — CASE NUMBERS DELIBERATELY NOT STATED, UNVERIFIED).

checklist.item: AUDIT ADDITION — Secure payments and e-money authorisation, or a regulated partner, before building any cash-in/cash-out flow
checklist.issuer: National competent authority under PSD2/EMD2 (or the chosen PSP/EMI partner's regulator)
checklist.appliesTo: B, C (and any model where prizes are money)
checklist.prerequisite: Decision on whether player funds are held by FACT//DUEL or by a regulated partner
checklist.notes: AUDIT ADDITION — entirely absent from the uncorrected brief, which covered AML in detail and payments not at all. Every model with a cash-out requires holding and remitting player funds, which triggers PSD2/EMD2 authorisation or the use of a regulated PSP/e-money institution, plus player-fund segregation obligations that are LICENCE CONDITIONS in Denmark, the Netherlands, Sweden, Spain and Malta. PSD3/PSR are in negotiation. A founder could build the entire gambling-compliance stack and still be unable to move money. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS ARE UNVERIFIED and out of this lane — but this is a hard build dependency, not a finance line item.

checklist.item: AUDIT ADDITION — Price the real licence-cost floors in every recommended market before committing to a licensing strategy
checklist.issuer: Founder / finance
checklist.cost: The point of the item is that this is currently unknown. KNOWN OR REPORTED FLOORS: Malta application EUR 5,000 + annual EUR 10,000 (solely Type 4) or EUR 25,000 (B2C incl. Type 3) + compliance contribution minimum EUR 5,000 (Type 4) or EUR 25,000 (Type 3) — VERIFIED. Italy per-concession fee reported around EUR 7m for nine years — UNVERIFIED. Romania minimum annual authorisation tax reported at EUR 480,000 — UNVERIFIED AND CONTESTED. Greece, Portugal and Czech bank-guarantee requirements — UNVERIFIED. Germany, Spain, Netherlands, Ireland, Denmark, Sweden — NO FEE FIGURE VERIFIED FOR ANY OF THEM.
checklist.notes: AUDIT ADDITION. The uncorrected brief recommended a licensing strategy while disclosing a realistic cost for exactly one market (Malta). Licence ECONOMICS, not licence availability, will determine the realistic EU footprint for an early-stage product. Get the fee schedules before the legal opinions; a market you cannot afford does not need an opinion.

checklist.item: AUDIT ADDITION — Check advertising and marketing restrictions in every target market before assuming a licence makes the market addressable
checklist.issuer: National gambling regulators and advertising authorities
checklist.leadTime: Before any user-acquisition budget is committed
checklist.notes: AUDIT ADDITION — entirely absent from the uncorrected brief and decisive for a consumer app. Italy operates a near-total gambling advertising ban (Decreto Dignita). Spain restricts gambling advertising under Real Decreto 958/2020. The Netherlands bans untargeted gambling advertising. Belgium introduced an advertising prohibition in 2023-24. Germany imposes advertising limits under the GlueStV. A licensed Model C in these markets could be perfectly legal to operate and effectively impossible to market. ALL DETAIL UNVERIFIED — but the existence of these regimes is not in doubt, and the user-acquisition model must be tested against them before a licence is bought.

checklist.item: AUDIT ADDITION — Map local establishment, local representative and local tax registration requirements before filing anywhere
checklist.issuer: National gambling regulators
checklist.prerequisite: Chosen EU establishment (Malta, on the current plan)
checklist.notes: AUDIT ADDITION. Several regimes require an EEA-established entity with local tax registration before an application is even accepted, and several require a local presence or representative. CONFIRMED IN THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF: Slovakia requires a Slovak-seated registered representative; Poland requires a Polish seat or office. UNVERIFIED BUT TO BE ASSUMED: equivalent requirements in Hungary, Czechia, Greece and Romania. This changes the entity structure, not just the paperwork — a single Maltese company may not be a sufficient EU vehicle.

checklist.item: AUDIT ADDITION — Model player-winnings withholding tax and gambling VAT treatment at the payout layer, not as a finance line
checklist.issuer: National tax authorities
checklist.leadTime: Before any payout code is written
checklist.notes: AUDIT ADDITION. Spain, Romania, Greece and Portugal apply withholding taxes on player winnings and/or specific VAT treatment of gambling supplies. These change prize-pool economics AND require product changes at the payout layer — withholding, reporting and net-vs-gross display to the player. ALL RATES AND MECHANICS UNVERIFIED. Separately, Malta's VAT exemption for gambling changes from 1 October 2026 alongside the gaming tax change — OUT OF LANE, UNANALYSED, but relevant to the Maltese establishment decision.

checklist.item: AUDIT ADDITION — Check the prize-competition and promotional-game regimes that sit OUTSIDE gambling law in the 'Camp 1' states
checklist.issuer: National consumer/advertising authorities; Kansspelautoriteit (for the Dutch code)
checklist.leadTime: Before any paid contest launches in a Camp 1 state
checklist.notes: AUDIT ADDITION, correcting a false implication of the uncorrected brief: escaping gambling law does not mean no regime applies. The Dutch Gedragscode promotionele kansspelen, Austrian Preisausschreiben rules and national unfair-commercial-practice rules on paid entry contests all bite on products that are outside gambling law. Germany's § 33d GewO (see the German item) is the sharpest example. NONE of the Camp 1 states is a regulatory vacuum. ALL DETAIL UNVERIFIED.

checklist.item: AUDIT ADDITION — Build age verification and minor protection for Models A and D independently of gambling law
checklist.issuer: DSA enforcement (Commission/national Digital Services Coordinators); national youth-media authorities
checklist.notes: AUDIT ADDITION. The uncorrected brief said of Model D that 'no gambling-law authority is engaged' and stopped there. The DSA's minor-protection provisions, the German JuSchG and national youth-media law apply to Model A and Model D regardless. The CPC virtual-currency principles also specifically address direct exhortation to children and time-limited purchase pressure — which is what the Star Stable enforcement action was about. SPECIFIC OBLIGATIONS UNVERIFIED and out of this lane, but this is a launch-blocking build item for a consumer app with a virtual currency.

checklist.item: AUDIT ADDITION — Maintain a per-subdivision verification register recording method and date of check
checklist.issuer: Self-imposed
checklist.notes: AUDIT ADDITION. Roughly half the 27 member-state entries in the uncorrected brief carried UNVERIFIED statute citations with no article numbers, and seven (Bulgaria, Croatia, Estonia, Hungary, Lithuania, Slovakia, Slovenia) rested on a single 2026 gambling-regulators directory — yet all 27 read with equal apparent authority. In this corrected edition each subdivision's authority line states its verification status explicitly. PRIMARY-TEXT-CHECKED THIS LANE: Denmark (danskelove.dk), Spain (BOE consolidated text), Sweden (Spellag text, including the kombinationsspel definition), Germany § 33d GewO (gesetze-im-internet.de), the AMLR (EUR-Lex), the Commission's online gambling page, and the MGA fee guidance note. EVERYTHING ELSE IS SECONDARY OR UNVERIFIED.

checklist.item: Commission a per-market local-counsel opinion before taking money from any member state
checklist.issuer: Local gambling counsel in each target member state
checklist.prerequisite: Frozen product spec — timer, question draw, RAKE STRUCTURE (operator-funded fixed pool vs commission on a player-funded pot), prize structure, currency flows
checklist.notes: THIS DOCUMENT IS A COMPLIANCE CHECKLIST, NOT LEGAL ADVICE. Every Model C verdict turns on a skill-versus-chance assessment that only a local regulator or court can settle, fact-specific to the exact duel format. CORRECTED PRIORITY ORDER: Germany (largest market, best carve-out, and the § 33d GewO question that the uncorrected brief missed entirely — highest downside if wrong), Sweden (the audit reversed this market from 'exempt' to 'licence likely required' — confirm before any Nordic plan), Ireland (new regime, clearest capture of skill, and every Irish date in this document is unverified), Spain and Italy (skill expressly captured; Italy also needs the concession fee confirmed before it is worth an opinion at all), Netherlands (carve-out available but appellate authority runs against skill claims), Austria (reform details entirely unverified), France (confirm the geo-block; do not seek a route in).

subdivisions.name: EU level (horizontal) — AUDIT ADDITION
subdivisions.status: no licence, but binding horizontal obligations
subdivisions.detail: There is no EU gambling licence, no EU gambling regulator and no mutual recognition. What IS directly applicable EU-wide: (1) AMLR Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 from 10 July 2027 — providers of gambling services are obliged entities (Art. 3(3)(g)); CDD on collection of winnings, wagering of a stake, or both, at EUR 2,000 or more (ART. 19(5), corrected from the uncorrected brief's Art. 20(5)); Art. 4 lets member states exempt low-risk gambling services, with an exclusion for providers whose principal activity is online gambling or sport betting BUT WITH A CARVE-BACK for state-operated and state-regulated online gambling, and subject to a Member State risk assessment and Commission process; whether a genuinely chance-free Model C is an AMLR 'gambling service' at all is CONTESTED, because Art. 2(1)(12) still requires a game of chance. (2) CPC Network in-game virtual currency principles, 21 March 2025. (3) Digital Fairness Act, Commission work programme Q4 2026 — NOT YET TABLED as at 14 September 2026. (4) Digital Content Directive (EU) 2019/770, Consumer Rights Directive withdrawal right, DSA minor-protection provisions. (5) CJEU C-440/23 (16 April 2026): member states may prohibit online gambling licensed elsewhere and attach civil consequences including restitution. (6) OUT OF LANE BUT ENGAGED: PSD2/EMD2 payments and e-money authorisation, GDPR consequences of mandatory KYC, VAT on in-game currency.
subdivisions.authority: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Arts. 2(1)(12), 3(3)(g), 4, 19(5), 20(1)(a), 90, recitals 63-64 — EUR-Lex, PRIMARY, article numbers corrected per audit. Commission online gambling policy page — PRIMARY. CPC principles 21 March 2025 — PRIMARY. Digital Fairness Act Q4 2026 — EP Legislative Train, checked by editor. C-440/23 — SECONDARY (practitioner reporting; curia text not fetched).

subdivisions.name: Austria
subdivisions.status: split by model — Model C arguably outside gambling law; Model B not licensable today (STATUS CORRECTED from 'prohibited', which contradicted the brief's own Model C analysis)
subdivisions.detail: AUDIT CORRECTION TO THE STATUS LABEL: the uncorrected brief labelled Austria 'prohibited' while its own detail and Model C analysis placed Austria outside gambling law for a skill-predominant contest. A founder or engineer reading the subdivision table for geo-blocking decisions would have got the opposite instruction from the narrative. CORRECTED: Model C — GSpG § 1(1) captures only games where the outcome depends exclusively or predominantly on chance ('ausschliesslich oder vorwiegend vom Zufall'), so a genuinely skill-predominant contest is arguably outside gambling law; STATUTORY TEXT UNVERIFIED (never fetched by researcher or auditor) and the 5/7/10-second timer plus random question draw puts the predominance conclusion in real doubt. AUDIT ADDITION: Austrian Preisausschreiben / prize-competition rules and unfair-commercial-practice rules still apply to a paid contest outside gambling law — UNVERIFIED as to detail. Model B — cannot be licensed today; the online monopoly sits with Oesterreichische Lotterien. REFORM IN FLIGHT AND ENTIRELY UNVERIFIED: reports of a draft opening online gambling to multi-licensing (reportedly 20-30 licences), notified to the Commission in August 2026 after a consultation closing 15 July 2026, with unlicensed operators required to stop serving Austrians by 1 January 2027 or face an 18-month licensing exclusion rising to 24 months from 2030 — THE AUDITOR COULD NOT CONFIRM ANY ELEMENT OF THIS against TRIS or any primary source, and the 18/24-month exclusion is an unusually specific claim to rest on trade reporting. Do not make a geo-block or exit decision on the 1 January 2027 date without a TRIS notification number. subdivisions.name: France
subdivisions.status: caught — geo-block for any paid contest with a chance element (STATUS REASONING CORRECTED: France does not prohibit skill contests as a class)
subdivisions.detail: AUDIT CORRECTION TO THE HEADLINE CHARACTERISATION. The uncorrected brief called France 'THE CLEAREST NO IN THE EU, AND IT IS SPECIFICALLY A NO TO SKILL GAMES'. That overstates the provision. On the brief's own quoted text, Art. L320-1 CSI prohibits operations offered to the public 'pour faire naitre l'esperance d'un gain qui serait du, MEME PARTIELLEMENT, AU HASARD et pour lesquelles un sacrifice financier est exige', then adds: 'Cette interdiction recouvre les jeux dont le fonctionnement repose sur le savoir-faire des joueurs. Le sacrifice financier est etabli dans les cas ou une avance financiere est exigee de la part des participants, meme si un remboursement ulterieur est rendu possible par le reglement du jeu.' CHANCE REMAINS A CONSTITUENT ELEMENT. The savoir-faire sentence closes the skill-PREDOMINANCE escape for MIXED games; it does not prohibit paid contests decided wholly by knowledge or ability, and paid chess and bridge tournaments and quiz competitions continue lawfully in France. THE CORRECT STATEMENT: France catches any paid contest with ANY chance element — which on FACT//DUEL's own facts (randomly drawn questions, reflex timers) probably does catch it. The second sentence independently defeats Model B's free-alternative-entry structure. The only adjacent carve-out, video-game competitions at Arts. L321-8 to L321-11 CSI (Decret n° 2017-871 of 9 May 2017), applies only where participants are PHYSICALLY PRESENT and caps entry fees at a decreed fraction of total organisation cost (the percentage is UNVERIFIED and has not been guessed) — paid online competitions do not qualify. ANJ licences cover only sports betting, horse betting and online poker; online casino is prohibited. Models A and D are unaffected. PRACTICAL CONCLUSION UNCHANGED: geo-block France for the current product. A fully deterministic fixed-question no-timer format would need a French opinion rather than an assumption.

subdivisions.name: Germany
subdivisions.status: split by model — Model C outside the GlueStV if skill predominates BUT a § 33d GewO trade permit is engaged; Model B has no fitting permission class
subdivisions.detail: THE LARGEST EU MARKET AND THE MOST CHANGED ENTRY IN THIS CORRECTED EDITION. § 3(1) GlueStV 2021: gambling exists where 'im Rahmen eines Spiels fuer den Erwerb einer Gewinnchance ein Entgelt verlangt wird und die Entscheidung ueber den Gewinn ganz oder ueberwiegend vom Zufall abhaengt'. BOTH elements are needed, so a contest decided by intellectual performance is not Gluecksspiel even with an entry fee and § 284 StGB does not bite. AUDIT ADDITION AND THE DOCUMENT'S BIGGEST OMISSION: that does NOT mean no German permission is required. § 33d GewO requires an Erlaubnis from the competent authority for commercially operating 'andere Spiele mit Gewinnmoeglichkeit' — other games with a chance to win that are NOT Gluecksspiel — which is precisely the category a paid skill contest falls into when it escapes § 3(1) GlueStV; a Bundeskriminalamt Unbedenklichkeitsbescheinigung is a precondition and the permit must be refused where the applicant lacks the required reliability (provision verified at gesetze-im-internet.de, 14 Sep 2026). ITS APPLICATION TO PURELY ONLINE OFFERINGS IS CONTESTED — which is exactly why it must be in the German opinion rather than absent from the analysis. The uncorrected brief's advice to 'run Model C in Germany unlicensed' is WITHDRAWN. MODEL B — AUDIT CORRECTION: the uncorrected brief described the GGL's permission classes as exhaustive (sports betting § 21, online poker § 22b, virtual slot machines § 22a, lotteries, horse betting) and concluded Model B was 'unlicensable'. The GGL's own legal-basis page states GlueStV 2021 made licensable virtuelle Automatenspiele, Online-Poker UND ONLINECASINOSPIELE, and online casino games are authorised by the individual LAENDER through their own concession procedures, not by the GGL. The enumeration was incomplete and the categorical 'unlicensable' is withdrawn — the accurate statement is that no existing class fits a player-v-player knowledge stake, so the product cannot be licensed in its current shape, but restructuring into a licensable class is not categorically foreclosed. THE RISK THAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED: FACT//DUEL's 5/7/10-second timers on randomly drawn questions push the 'ueberwiegend vom Zufall' analysis toward chance. The GGL and the Laender must complete a statutory evaluation of GlueStV 2021 by 31 December 2026 (§ 32, section number SECONDARY); a reformed treaty would not take effect before roughly 2027-2028 (SECONDARY). Trade press reported a 'small adjustment' targeted for spring 2026 ratification — NOT CORROBORATED against any official source and NOT RELIED ON. AUDIT ADDITION: German advertising limits under the GlueStV, and JuSchG youth-protection duties, apply independently — UNVERIFIED as to detail. LICENCE/PERMIT FEES AND LEAD TIMES UNVERIFIED for both the GGL permission and the § 33d GewO Erlaubnis.

subdivisions.name: Ireland
subdivisions.status: licence-required (Model C as well as Model B) — BUT EVERY DATE AND THRESHOLD IN THIS ENTRY IS UNVERIFIED
subdivisions.detail: Ireland matters because its definition of gaming expressly catches skill: 'games of skill or chance (or partly of skill and partly of chance) where the participant pays money for the chance to win a prize of money (or money's worth)' — no skill carve-out, so Model C needs a licence just as Model B does. Lotteries are separately defined to include activities involving 'a guess of future events or of past events where the results are not generally known' — phrasing close enough to a trivia product to warrant specific counsel. AUDIT CORRECTION TO THE CONFIDENCE LEVEL, NOT THE CONCLUSION: the uncorrected brief called Ireland 'THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL NEW REGIME FOR THIS PRODUCT' while resting the entire verdict on a law-firm restatement of the s. 2 definitions and a six-date commencement timeline, none of it primary-sourced. irishstatutebook.ie, oireachtas.ie and grai.ie all returned 403 to both the researcher and the auditor. TREAT AS PROVISIONAL. The reported timeline — Act signed 23 October 2024; commencement order signed 3 February 2026 effective 5 February 2026; remote betting / remote betting intermediary / in-person betting applications opened 9 February 2026 via the GRAI Operator Portal; remote betting licence requirement from 1 July 2026; in-person from 1 December 2026 — is UNVERIFIED, though the betting dates are corroborated across DLA Piper, LexisNexis and gov.ie. REMOTE GAMING (B2C) LICENCES ARE REPORTED AS NOT YET OPEN — variously Q4 2026 or 2027-28; confirm with the GRAI. Reported as already in force: credit-card gambling ban, mandatory customer spending limits for remote gambling, child protection rules, suspicious-behaviour reporting (UNVERIFIED). Administrative sanctions reported up to EUR 20m or 10% of turnover (UNVERIFIED). B2B licensing also reportedly applies to software and hosting suppliers. subdivisions.detail: ITALY DOES NOT EXEMPT SKILL — IT LICENSES IT. D.M. 17 settembre 2007 n. 186, 'Regolamento per la disciplina dei giochi di abilita a distanza con vincita in denaro', governs remote skill games with cash prizes and expressly covers games where the result depends PREDOMINANTLY OVER the random element on the skill of the players. The remote sector was reordered by D.Lgs. 25 marzo 2024 n. 41 (in force 4 April 2024, implementing Art. 15 of Law 111/2023). AUDIT ADDITIONS, BOTH DECISIVE AND BOTH ABSENT FROM THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF: (1) D.Lgs. 41/2024 sets a multi-million-euro fee per remote concession, widely reported at around EUR 7m for a nine-year concession — FIGURE UNVERIFIED, but the order of magnitude removes Italy from an early-stage footprint, and listing Italy as an action item with cost 'UNVERIFIED' materially understated the barrier. (2) Italy operates a near-total gambling advertising ban under the Decreto Dignita, so a licensed Italian product could be legal to operate and impossible to market. CONTESTED: the reported award of 52 concessions to 46 operators in September 2025 with a 5-concession cap per operator could not be confirmed by the auditor. Regulator: Agenzia delle Dogane e dei Monopoli (ADM).

subdivisions.name: Malta
subdivisions.status: licence-required — the pragmatic establishment choice, with a hard ceiling and a corrected legal basis
subdivisions.detail: CITATION CORRECTED — THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF CITED A REPEALED INSTRUMENT AS THE LIVE REGIME. The Skill Games Regulations (S.L. 438.11), in force 24 January 2017 under the Lotteries and Other Games Act (Cap. 438), were repealed by Act XVI of 2018, the Gaming Act (Cap. 583), which replaced Cap. 438 and its subsidiary legislation. DO NOT CITE S.L. 438.11. The current instruments are the Gaming Act Cap. 583 and its subsidiary legislation (the MGA's regulatory-framework page lists S.L. 583.3-583.12; the Gaming Authorisations Regulations are reported as S.L. 583.05, NOT 438.11 — S.L. NUMBER UNVERIFIED). THE SUBSTANTIVE CONCEPT SURVIVES: a controlled skill game is still a recognised category under Cap. 583 and MGA Directive 6 of 2018 ('Controlled Skill Games Ruling', 1 August 2018), which does exist. A skill game is a game for money or money's worth offered by distance communication whose result is determined by skill alone or predominantly by skill. THE TYPE 3 / TYPE 4 CHOICE IS A CHARACTERISATION WITH EU-WIDE CONSEQUENCES — AUDIT CORRECTION: the uncorrected brief said the 'likelier fit' for duels is Type 3 ('games of chance not played against the house and wherein the operator is not exposed to gaming risk' — P2P with a rake) without flagging that Type 3 is by definition a class of GAMES OF CHANCE. Filing for Type 3 concedes the product is a game of chance, which destroys the skill-predominance argument in Germany and Austria, weakens it in the Netherlands, and strengthens capture in Denmark, Sweden, Spain, Ireland and Italy. Type 3 and Type 4 are not interchangeable fallbacks. THE GAP: under Directive 6 of 2018, fantasy sports remains the only game the MGA has classified as a controlled skill game, so a trivia duel needs a fresh MGA determination and the burden of proving skill predominance is on the applicant — budget for a pre-application ruling request. COSTS (MGA guidance note, Dec 2024 v3, VERIFIED): application fee EUR 5,000; fixed annual licence fee EUR 10,000 if providing solely Type 4, otherwise EUR 25,000 for a B2C gaming service licence; Type 4 compliance contribution min EUR 5,000 / max EUR 500,000 at 0.50% rising to 2.00% by band; Type 3 min EUR 25,000 / max EUR 500,000 at 4.00% tapering to 0.40%; minimum share capital EUR 40,000 for Types 3 and 4, EUR 100,000 for Types 1-2. GAMING TAX — AUDIT FLAGGED AS POSSIBLY FABRICATED; EDITOR VERIFIED IT IS REAL: from 1 OCTOBER 2026 (A FUTURE DATE as at 14 September 2026) the single 5% rate is replaced by 15% of aggregate gaming revenue for Type 1 and 10% for Types 2, 3 and 4, with 5% retained for controlled gaming premises and junkets; the device-based levy is abolished and a higher fixed studio broadcasting levy introduced. MATERIAL AND PREVIOUSLY MISSED: for distance gaming the taxability test changes from the player's PHYSICAL PRESENCE in Malta to whether the player is established, has a permanent address and/or usually resides in Malta — the old 'only players physically in Malta' shorthand no longer states the rule. THE LEGAL NOTICE NUMBERS (reported as LN 84/2026 and LN 86/2026) REMAIN UNVERIFIED. A separate VAT change also takes effect 1 October 2026 — out of lane. CEILING: an MGA licence does NOT passport. Bill 55 (2023) inserting Art. 56A into the Gaming Act — requiring Maltese courts to refuse recognition of foreign judgments against MGA licensees — drew a Commission letter of formal notice, and in Case C-440/23 (16 April 2026) the CJEU held a member state may prohibit online gambling licensed elsewhere and may allow players to recover losses. LEAD TIME UNVERIFIED — no MGA service-level commitment exists; consultancy estimates of 4-6 months are marketing material.

subdivisions.name: Netherlands
subdivisions.status: licence-required for Model B; Model C contested and the appellate weather runs against skill claims
subdivisions.detail: AUDIT CORRECTION — THE NETHERLANDS IS LESS FAVOURABLE THAN THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF IMPLIED. Art. 1(1)(a) Wet op de kansspelen prohibits, without a licence, giving an opportunity to compete for prizes where winners are determined by a chance mechanism on which participants generally cannot exert 'overwegende invloed' (decisive influence). A genuine behendigheidsspel is outside the Act. The uncorrected brief presented this as a live 50/50 by setting the Hoge Raad's 1998 poker ruling against a 2010 Hague District Court decision the other way. THAT 2010 DECISION WAS REVERSED ON APPEAL by the Gerechtshof Den Haag, and Dutch higher courts have consistently maintained that poker is a kansspel under the Wok. The honest framing: the 'overwegende invloed' test has been applied AGAINST skill claims at appellate level, so the Netherlands is a contested market for Model C, not a Camp 1 safe harbour. Wok statutory text was NEVER FETCHED by researcher or auditor (SECONDARY). Current licensing: Wet Kansspelen op afstand; new policy rules BVRKOA 2026 in force 1 January 2026; the September 2021 cohort of licences EXPIRES 1 OCTOBER 2026 — A FUTURE EVENT as at the date of this correction; licences run a maximum of 5 years; applicants must submit an exit plan and a change-notification plan. The KSA's 2026 Toezichtagenda prioritises illegal supply, working through an alliance with payment service providers, social media and hosting companies — a grey-market launch will be found. AUDIT ADDITIONS: the Gedragscode promotionele kansspelen governs promotional games outside the Wok; the Netherlands operates an untargeted-gambling-advertising ban; player-fund segregation is a licence condition. ALL THREE UNVERIFIED AS TO DETAIL. The KSA's 'Leidraad beoordeling kansspelen' could not be retrieved (404), and the KSA's current position on virtual currencies and paid skill games specifically is UNVERIFIED. Fees and lead times UNVERIFIED.

subdivisions.status: licence-required — and CONTESTED as to the economics that would disqualify it
subdivisions.detail: Licensing market. THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF DISQUALIFIED ROMANIA ON A SINGLE UNVERIFIED NUMBER. It stated that from 1 August 2025 the authorisation tax on online gambling rose from 21% to 30% of gambling revenues and the minimum annual authorisation tax rose to EUR 480,000 — 'a figure that alone disqualifies an early-stage product'. THE AUDITOR COULD NOT CONFIRM EITHER FIGURE against any primary source, notes that the Romanian rate is reported elsewhere at figures other than 30%, and flags that the EUR 480,000 minimum is a decision-grade number resting entirely on secondary reporting. TREAT AS CONTESTED: Romania's cost floor is probably high enough to disqualify it for an early-stage product, but verify ONJN orders before recording that as a fact. Other reported items, all SECONDARY: ONJN leadership was reset in April 2025; the regulator has pursued repeated blacklisting of unlicensed sites and stated that unlicensed 'counterparty betting' will be treated as regulated gambling requiring full authorisation; a centralised self-exclusion register is expected in 2026 (President's Order no. 79/2025); Order 33/2025 defines notifiable 'significant changes'. AUDIT ADDITIONS: Romania applies withholding tax on player winnings (UNVERIFIED) and local establishment requirements should be assumed (UNVERIFIED). subdivisions.name: Spain
subdivisions.detail: SKILL PREDOMINANCE IS NO DEFENCE ONCE A CHANCE ELEMENT IS PRESENT — WHICH IS NARROWER THAN 'NO PURE-SKILL EXEMPTION'. AUDIT CORRECTION: Art. 3(a) Ley 13/2011 defines 'juego' as any activity in which money or economically valuable objects are risked on uncertain future results 'DEPENDIENTES EN ALGUNA MEDIDA DEL AZAR' — dependent TO SOME DEGREE ON CHANCE — permitting transfer between participants, 'con independencia de que predomine en ellos el grado de habilidad, destreza o pericia de los jugadores o sean exclusiva o primordialmente de suerte, envite o azar'. The 'independencia de que predomine la habilidad' clause means skill-predominance is no defence once chance is present; it does NOT capture a contest with no chance element at all. The uncorrected brief's flat 'Spain expressly has NO pure-skill exemption' overstated this. For FACT//DUEL the practical answer is unchanged — the random question draw supplies the chance element — but the reasoning must be stated correctly. SECOND AUDIT CORRECTION: THE GENERAL-LICENCE CATEGORIES (apuestas, rifas, concursos, otros juegos) SIT IN ARTICLE 10, NOT ARTICLE 9. 'Concursos' is defined at Art. 3(e) as offers made through media (TV, radio, internet) requiring an economic outlay with prizes determined by chance, competition or knowledge tests — WHETHER AN APP-BASED DUEL FITS THAT DEFINITION IS UNTESTED and is a specific question for Spanish counsel, which the uncorrected brief never asked. Art. 2.2 excludes only games or competitions 'de puro ocio, pasatiempo o recreo que constituyan usos sociales' with no economically evaluable transfers, and excludes promotional combinations with random elements. A general licence must be held before the matching singular licence can be sought; general licences are awarded through a public convocatoria, not on demand. AUDIT ADDITIONS: Real Decreto 958/2020 severely restricts gambling advertising; player-winnings withholding tax and gambling VAT treatment change prize-pool economics and require payout-layer product changes; player-fund segregation is a licence condition. ALL THREE UNVERIFIED AS TO DETAIL. The DGOJ was consulting on amendments to Ley 13/2011 as at July 2026 (SECONDARY). Fees and lead times UNVERIFIED. VERIFICATION STATUS: PRIMARY TEXT CHECKED (BOE consolidated text).
