subdivisions.name: Sweden
subdivisions.status: licence-required — REVERSED BY THE AUDIT from the uncorrected brief's 'outside gambling law'
subdivisions.detail: THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL SUBDIVISION REVERSAL IN THIS CORRECTED EDITION. The uncorrected brief placed Sweden in the 'outside gambling law, no licence' camp in its headline and Model C analysis, on the strength of a Spelinspektionen page about competitions decided by a prestationsmoment — while its own subdivision row simultaneously said 'licence-required'. A founder reading the headline would have launched paid contests in Sweden unlicensed. CORRECTED POSITION: Spellagen defines KOMBINATIONSSPEL as 'spel dar deltagarna har chans att vinna ett pris och dar sannolikheten att vinna beror pa en kombination av skicklighet och slump' — a game where participants have a chance to win a prize and the probability of winning depends on a COMBINATION OF SKILL AND CHANCE — and kombinationsspel is a licensable form of spel, structurally identical to the Danish kombinationsspil the brief already treated as fatal (definition verified against the Spellag text, 14 Sep 2026). The Spelinspektionen carve-out is strict on its own wording: it exempts only competitions where the winner is decided by a performance element 'UTAN INSLAG AV LOTTNING ELLER SLUMP' — WITHOUT any element of drawing lots or chance, not merely 'predominantly skill'. A randomly drawn question set introduces exactly the inslag av slump that defeats it. ON ITS OWN FACTS FACT//DUEL'S PAID DUEL IS A CANDIDATE SWEDISH KOMBINATIONSSPEL REQUIRING A SPELINSPEKTIONEN LICENCE. A Swedish Model C would need an identical fixed question set for every entrant, no random matching, and no chance-introducing timer — and even then a Swedish opinion. Other exemptions at 3 kap. 4-5 §§ Spellagen: FREE-TO-ENTER GAMES (3 kap. 4 § — 'licens kravs inte for spel dar deltagande inte kraver betalning av en insats'), private play between close connections, combination games in periodicals/radio/TV, and municipal non-profit lotteries. Model B requires a Spelinspektionen licence. AUDIT ADDITION: player-fund segregation is a Swedish licence condition — DETAIL UNVERIFIED. An amending act SFS 2025:767 exists and ITS CONTENT IS ENTIRELY UNVERIFIED — it could affect this position. Fees and lead times UNVERIFIED. VERIFICATION STATUS: PRIMARY TEXT CHECKED for the kombinationsspel definition and the no-stake exemption.
subdivisions.authority: Spellag (2018:1138), in force 1 January 2019 — kombinationsspel definition and 3 kap. 4-5 §§ exemptions, verified against the Spellag text 14 Sep 2026 (riksdagen.se / svenskforfattningssamling.se). Spelforordning (2018:1475). Spelinspektionen guidance page 'Nar kravs det inte licens?' fetched 14 Sep 2026 — NOTE the guidance is narrower than the uncorrected brief read it. SFS 2025:767 — CONTENT UNVERIFIED. Regulator: Spelinspektionen.

risks: GERMANY WAS THE BRIEF'S RECOMMENDED FIRST MARKET AND THE BRIEF MISSED THE PERMIT THAT APPLIES THERE. Escaping § 3(1) GlueStV on skill predominance does not mean no German permission is needed: § 33d GewO requires a trade permit (Erlaubnis) for commercially operating 'andere Spiele mit Gewinnmoeglichkeit' — games with a chance to win that are NOT Gluecksspiel — which is exactly where a paid skill contest lands. Its application to purely online offerings is CONTESTED. The uncorrected advice to 'run Model C in Germany unlicensed' is withdrawn; get a German opinion covering both provisions before charging a single German player.

SWEDEN IS A LICENCE MARKET FOR THIS PRODUCT, NOT AN EXEMPT ONE. Spellagen's kombinationsspel — a game where the probability of winning depends on a combination of skill and chance — is licensable, and the Spelinspektionen carve-out the uncorrected brief relied on requires the ABSENCE of any element of chance, not skill predominance. A random question draw defeats it. The uncorrected headline would have sent a founder into Sweden unlicensed.

MODEL B IS STILL NOT LAUNCHABLE EU-WIDE, BUT NOT FOR THE REASON PREVIOUSLY GIVEN. The uncorrected claim that 'no EU member state uses a consideration gateway' is wrong — Spellagen 3 kap. 4 § exempts games requiring no stake, and Germany's test asks whether an Entgelt is demanded. Genuinely free-to-enter designs DO work in specific states. What no EU state accepts is a DUAL paid-plus-free entry route cleansing the paid route, and France defeats it in terms. Do not dismiss free-entry designs; do not assume a free side door launders a paid product.

THE MALTA TYPE 3 / TYPE 4 CHOICE IS AN EU-WIDE CHARACTERISATION, NOT A FORM CHOICE. Type 3 is by definition a class of GAMES OF CHANCE. Filing for Type 3 concedes the product is a game of chance and destroys the skill-predominance argument in Germany and Austria, weakens it in the Netherlands and strengthens capture in Denmark, Sweden, Spain, Ireland and Italy. The uncorrected brief presented Type 3 and Type 4 as interchangeable fallbacks.

THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF CITED A REPEALED MALTESE INSTRUMENT AS THE LIVE SKILL-GAMES REGIME. S.L. 438.11 was repealed by the Gaming Act (Cap. 583), Act XVI of 2018. The controlled-skill-game concept survives under Cap. 583 and MGA Directive 6 of 2018, but any filing or investor document citing S.L. 438.11 is citing law that has not existed for years.

THE AMLR ITEM WAS LABELLED 'VERIFIED PRIMARY TEXT' AND CONTAINED TWO CITATION ERRORS AND ONE OVERSTATEMENT. The CDD provision is Art. 19(5), not Art. 20(5). The Art. 4 exemption has a carve-back for state-operated and state-regulated online gambling that the brief truncated away, so 'FACT//DUEL cannot be exempted' is withdrawn. And AMLR capture of a genuinely chance-free Model C is CONTESTED, because Art. 2(1)(12) still requires a 'game of chance' — the brief could not simultaneously argue Model C is chance-free enough to escape the GlueStV and that it is an AMLR game of chance. Build the KYC stack anyway; the engineering conclusion survives the legal correction.

PAYMENTS AND E-MONEY AUTHORISATION IS A HARD BUILD DEPENDENCY AND WAS ENTIRELY ABSENT. Every model with a cash-out requires holding and remitting player funds, triggering PSD2/EMD2 authorisation or a regulated PSP/EMI partner, plus player-fund segregation obligations that are licence conditions in DK, NL, SE, ES and MT. A founder could build the whole gambling-compliance stack and still be unable to move money.

THE DOCUMENT RECOMMENDS A LICENSING STRATEGY WHILE KNOWING THE PRICE OF EXACTLY ONE MARKET. Malta's fees are verified. Germany, Spain, Italy, the Netherlands, Ireland, Denmark and Sweden are all UNVERIFIED. Italy's per-concession fee is reported around EUR 7m for nine years and Romania's minimum annual authorisation tax at EUR 480,000 — both UNVERIFIED, and either would remove the market. Licence ECONOMICS, not licence availability, will set the realistic EU footprint.

A LICENSED MARKET CAN STILL BE AN UNMARKETABLE ONE. Italy's near-total advertising ban (Decreto Dignita), Spain's Real Decreto 958/2020, the Dutch untargeted-advertising ban, Belgium's 2023-24 prohibition and Germany's GlueStV advertising limits were absent from the uncorrected brief. For a consumer app that depends on paid acquisition this is decisive and should be checked before a licence is bought.

THE RAKE STRUCTURE IS A BIGGER LEVER THAN THE TIMER AND WAS NEVER ANALYSED. Taking a commission from a player-funded pot makes the product a Type 3 P2P game in Malta and a 'stake' under most EU definitions; paying a fixed, announced, operator-funded prize pool that does not depend on entrant numbers weakens or removes the stake limb in several states. That is the difference between licensable and out-of-scope in Germany, Austria and the Netherlands. Freeze this before instructing counsel.

THE 5/7/10-SECOND TIMER IS A LEGAL DESIGN DECISION, NOT A GAME-FEEL DECISION. Every favourable Model C verdict in Germany, Austria and the Netherlands depends on a skill-versus-chance test, and Sweden's and France's tests are stricter still — they turn on the ABSENCE of chance, not its non-predominance. Short timers on randomly drawn questions convert knowledge into reflex and draw-luck. Fixed identical question sets, longer timers and larger samples per contest all buy legal ground; the current duel format spends it.

AN MGA LICENCE BUYS ESTABLISHMENT, NOT MARKET ACCESS, AND THE DOWNSIDE IS RESTITUTION, NOT A FINE. There is no mutual recognition. In Case C-440/23 (European Lotto and Betting Ltd and Deutsche Lotto- und Sportwetten Ltd, judgment 16 April 2026) the CJEU held that a member state may prohibit online gambling licensed elsewhere, that member states may attach civil-law consequences including contract nullity and restitution of lost stakes, and that a player's restitution claim is not an abuse of EU rights. NOTE: the audit flagged this case as possibly fabricated; the editor verified it exists and the holdings are as described across multiple practitioner sources, though the curia text itself was not fetched. Malta's Art. 56A shield does not protect against a German, Dutch or Austrian claim.

THE 'ENTRIES' WORD IN MODEL A IS AN UNEXAMINED TRAPDOOR. If coins buy entry to anything carrying a prize of money or money's worth, Model A is Model C with a currency layer and every Model C analysis applies. Define precisely what an entry buys before treating Model A as safe.

BELGIUM CAN CRIMINALISE MODEL A IF COINS BUY RANDOMISED REWARDS. The Belgian Kansspelcommissie's 2018 position treats paid virtual currency plus chance plus an item of value as illegal gambling under the Gaming Act of 7 May 1999, enforced by threat of criminal prosecution. NOTE the audit's correction: this was a research report / position paper, not a formal adjudicative ruling, and its text is UNVERIFIED. No loot boxes, no gacha, no randomised paid rewards in the EU build regardless.

A SUBSCRIPTION CAN BE THE CONSIDERATION THAT CREATES GAMBLING. The MGA's controlled-skill-game definition counts consideration 'whether in the form of a stake, a periodic subscription or the purchase of in-game items, which provides an advantage to the player'. If the Model D subscription grants extra expedition entries, higher stake tiers or any competitive edge in a prize event, Model D converts into Model C. Keep it strictly cosmetic and strictly severed from prize contests.

SEVERAL REGIMES ARE MID-FLIGHT AND SOME OF THE DATES IN THIS DOCUMENT HAVE NOT HAPPENED YET — THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF WROTE TWO OF THEM IN THE COMPLETED PAST TENSE. As at 14 September 2026: Malta's gaming tax change takes effect 1 OCTOBER 2026 (future); the Netherlands' 2021 licence cohort expires 1 OCTOBER 2026 (future); Germany's GlueStV statutory evaluation is due 31 December 2026; the Digital Fairness Act is a Q4 2026 work-programme item NOT YET TABLED; Ireland's remote gaming licences are reported as not yet open; Finland's licensed market opens 1 July 2027; the AMLR applies from 10 July 2027. Austria's entire 2026 reform timeline is UNVERIFIED and should not be planned against. Re-verify every date before committing engineering or capital.

HALF THIS DOCUMENT'S SUBDIVISIONS ARE DIRECTORY-DERIVED AND SHOULD NOT BE READ WITH EQUAL AUTHORITY. Only Denmark, Spain, Sweden, Germany's § 33d GewO, the AMLR, the Commission's policy page and the MGA fee guidance were checked against primary text in this lane. Bulgaria, Croatia, Estonia, Hungary, Lithuania, Slovakia and Slovenia rest on a single 2026 regulators directory. Act names, article numbers and amendment status for those states are NOT reliable.

THIS IS A COMPLIANCE CHECKLIST, NOT LEGAL ADVICE. Every Model C verdict turns on a fact-specific skill-versus-chance assessment that only a national regulator or court can settle. Local counsel is required in every market before money is taken — corrected priority order: Germany, Sweden, Ireland, Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Austria, and France (to confirm the geo-block rather than to seek a route in).

WHETHER IT APPLIES TO A PURELY ONLINE OFFERING IS CONTESTED AND UNRESOLVED. This is the single most important open question in the German analysis and must be put to German counsel explicitly.

AMLR SCOPE OVER A CHANCE-FREE MODEL C: Art. 2(1)(12) requires 'wagering a stake with monetary value in games of chance, including those with an element of skill'. Whether a contest with NO chance element is an AMLR gambling service at all is CONTESTED. The safe engineering assumption is to build the KYC stack; the legal position is not settled.

AUSTRIA'S ENTIRE 2026 REFORM: the August 2026 Commission notification, the reported 20-30 licences, the 15 July 2026 consultation close, the 1 January 2027 exit deadline and the 18-month (rising to 24 from 2030) exclusion period could NOT be confirmed by the auditor against TRIS or any primary source. ROMANIA'S ECONOMICS: the reported rise of the online authorisation tax from 21% to 30% of gambling revenues from 1 August 2025 and the EUR 480,000 minimum annual authorisation tax could not be confirmed against any primary source; the rate is reported elsewhere at other figures. The EUR 480,000 number was used to disqualify an entire market. Verify ONJN orders before relying either way.

The per-concession fee under D.Lgs. 41/2024 — widely reported around EUR 7m for nine years — is UNVERIFIED but is the decision-grade number for Italy. The Decreto Dignita advertising ban is real in outline but UNVERIFIED as to current scope.

IRELAND: every date and threshold in the Irish entry is UNVERIFIED. irishstatutebook.ie, oireachtas.ie and grai.ie returned 403 to both the original researcher and the auditor. The s. 2 definitions on which the whole Irish verdict turns are quoted only through a law-firm guide. Betting dates are corroborated across DLA Piper, LexisNexis and gov.ie; the remote GAMING licence opening date is reported variously as Q4 2026 or 2027-28. The quoted wording (including 'meme partiellement, au hasard', 'recouvre les jeux dont le fonctionnement repose sur le savoir-faire des joueurs' and 'meme si un remboursement ulterieur est rendu possible') came through a search-engine rendering. High confidence, NOT primary. The percentage cap on entry fees in Decret n° 2017-871 is UNVERIFIED and has not been guessed.

NETHERLANDS: the Wok Art. 1(1)(a) text was never fetched. The audit's point that the 2010 Rechtbank 's-Gravenhage decision was reversed by the Gerechtshof Den Haag is accepted as the corrected position but THE APPEAL CITATION ITSELF IS UNVERIFIED. The KSA's 'Leidraad beoordeling kansspelen' could not be retrieved (404) and the KSA's current position on virtual currencies and paid skill games is UNVERIFIED.
SWEDEN SFS 2025:767: an amending act to the Spellagen exists; ITS CONTENT IS ENTIRELY UNVERIFIED and could affect the kombinationsspel or competition position either way.

MALTA: the Gaming Authorisations Regulations S.L. number (reported 583.05) and the reg. 8 controlled-skill-game cross-reference could not be verified from primary text — legislation.mt served only metadata to the auditor. The Gaming Tax (Amendment) Regulations 2026 are VERIFIED as to substance and commencement (1 October 2026; 15% Type 1, 10% Types 2-4) but the LEGAL NOTICE NUMBERS (reported LN 84/2026 and LN 86/2026) ARE UNVERIFIED. The change of the distance-gaming taxability test from physical presence to establishment/permanent address/usual residence is reported by PwC Malta and the MTCA press release and MATERIALLY AFFECTS THE ECONOMICS — confirm with Maltese tax counsel. CJEU C-440/23: the case IS real — European Lotto and Betting Ltd and Deutsche Lotto- und Sportwetten Ltd, judgment 16 April 2026, AG Emiliou opinion 4 September 2025 (CELEX 62023CC0440) — verified by the editor against GTG Advocates, Gecic Law, Mondaq, BSP and AGB reporting, contrary to the audit's suspicion of fabrication. THE JUDGMENT TEXT ITSELF WAS NOT FETCHED FROM CURIA.EUROPA.EU, so the exact holdings remain secondary. Verify on curia before using it in any filing or investor document.

DIGITAL FAIRNESS ACT TIMING: the audit suggested Q3 2026; the editor checked the European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, which records the DFA as a Q4 2026 initiative. Q4 2026 retained. As at 14 September 2026 no proposal has been tabled, so all reported scope (loot-box ban or parental consent, real-money price display) is pre-legislative and SECONDARY.

corrections: CERTAIN — AMLR CDD article renumbered: the customer-due-diligence trigger for gambling providers at the EUR 2,000 threshold is Article 19(5) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1624, NOT Article 20(5). Article 20 lists the CDD measures; Art. 19(5) cross-refers to Art. 20(1)(a). The error sat inside an item the brief labelled 'VERIFIED PRIMARY TEXT'. Corrected in the AMLR checklist item, the EU-level subdivision and the risks.

CERTAIN — AMLR Art. 4 carve-back restored: the brief truncated Art. 4(1) mid-sentence. The exclusion of online-gambling-principal-activity providers from member-state low-risk exemptions is followed by 'other than: (i) online gambling services operated by the State... (ii) online gambling services the organisation, operation and administration of which is regulated by the State' (recital 63 confirms). Exemptions also require a member-state risk assessment and a Commission step. The flat claim 'FACT//DUEL under Model B or C cannot be exempted' is WITHDRAWN.

The Spelinspektionen carve-out the brief relied on requires competitions to be decided 'utan inslag av lottning eller slump' — WITHOUT any element of chance. A random question draw defeats it. The categorical 'Model B is unlicensable in Germany' is softened to 'no existing class fits a P2P knowledge stake in its current shape'.

'THE CLEAREST NO IN THE EU, AND IT IS SPECIFICALLY A NO TO SKILL GAMES' is withdrawn; the corrected statement is that France catches any paid contest with ANY chance element, which on FACT//DUEL's facts probably does catch it.
